observation.visible_scene: A static macro side-view of a single cigarette resting horizontally on a dark, coarse granular surface (gravel-like) against a near-black background. From left to right the cigarette shows a tan/orange filter, a white-paper shaft, and a column of gray-white ash at the right end. The filter and the filter-to-paper boundary hold fixed positions throughout, indicating no camera motion and no translation of the cigarette body.
visible_changes: The burn line (boundary between white paper and ash) advances leftward over the excerpt: the white-paper section shortens while the ash column lengthens toward the left, with the far right tip of the ash staying at roughly the same horizontal position.

The ember at the burn line pulses in intensity rather than burning steadily: bright orange-red glow appears at certain frames (e.g. t≈0.07, 1.2, 2.2 s) and fades to a dim gray/dark line in between (e.g. t≈0.13–0.6, 0.8–1.0 s), consistent with an ongoing smolder.
Thin, faint wisps of smoke rise intermittently from the burn line and drift upward into the dark background (visible around t≈0, 0.47, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.6, 2.1, 2.3–2.5 s).
The ash texture shifts slightly frame to frame (small flakes/edges change shape), but no piece is seen detaching and falling.
The granular surface and black background remain unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the cigarette was lit before this segment and how much had already burned (the segment starts mid-burn).
What happens after the last frame (continued shortening, ash collapse, or extinguishing).
Whether the apparent leftward advance reflects real time or a sped-up/time-lapse capture.
The cause of the ember's brightness fluctuations (airflow, drawing, etc.).
uncertain_details: Exact burn rate and linearity of the leftward advance; the advance appears uneven between frames, possibly due to small ash shifts or measurement ambiguity at the burn line.
Whether minor changes in the ash outline are deformation, occlusion by smoke, or loss of a flake.
Precise position of the right ash tip over time (it looks roughly constant but may drift a few pixels).

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
